# PiP Clock

PiP Clock is a browser-based fullscreen analog clock published as a GitHub Pages site.

Canonical URL: https://saadchdhry.github.io/pages/
Repository: https://github.com/saadchdhry/pages

## What it is

This project is a minimalist, single-page clock designed to stay open as a pinned browser tab. The main workflow is helping the user move their currently active tab into Picture-in-Picture mode. That is especially helpful during video calls, remote meetings, screen sharing, and general video playback.

## Why someone would use it

Many browsers make Picture-in-Picture workflows easier when you have another tab ready to remain open in the main window. This page fills that role cleanly:

- It is visually quiet and distraction-free.
- It remains useful while idle because it shows the current time.
- It works well as a default tab to jump back to.
- It avoids clutter when a user wants their active meeting or video tab to float above other work.

## Additional helpful use cases

- A neutral standby tab during Google Meet, Zoom, Teams, or other browser-based calls
- A desktop companion clock during focused work
- A simple fullscreen clock for a secondary monitor
- A browser landing tab that is more useful than a blank page
- A low-distraction page for kiosk-like or ambient display setups
- A visual timing reference while watching recorded lectures or long-form videos

## Product characteristics

- Self-contained single-page HTML app
- Inline SVG analog clock rendering
- Light and dark theme handling
- Controls for marker visibility and stroke weight
- Continuous or ticking second-hand mode
- Calendar markers for month, day, and date
- No external runtime dependencies
